title: Concise Launchpad: single-row model scroller + request quick-capture
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Produce a compact, shareable screenshot bundle that showcases a slim, single-row model scroller (horizontal), an inline request quick-capture (lightweight builder), and three code snippet variants (curl minimal, Python async streaming, Node streaming + function call). These assets are for the Hosted API Getting Started page and the Console quickstart card.

Context: Existing starter screenshot packs are larger and focus on grid model pickers. For v2026.03 we want a reduced visual footprint optimized for docs and small marketing tiles while preserving key launch signals: model name, short capability badges, estimated price (microcopy), and a live-latency badge placeholder. The inline request quick-capture should show a composed prompt, a toggle for streaming (ON), and a compact function-calling hint ("uses functions: summarize") without exposing customer data.

Deliverables (image assets and specs):
- Model scroller (light + dark) 1200x280 PNG and 2x retina variants. Single horizontal row with 6 model cards visible, left chevron partially visible. Each card: model short-name, capability badge (chat/completions/embeddings), short tags (fast, low-cost), 2-line sample latency microcopy (e.g., "~70ms"), and token-cost microcopy (e.g., "est. $0.0009/token").
- Request quick-capture frame (light + dark) 1200x720 PNG: shows inline prompt, streaming toggle (ON), function call hint pill, sample token counter (45 tokens), and a "Run sample" button with spinner in a fake run state.
- Code snippet trio: curl-minimal.txt render 800x300 PNG, python-async-streaming.txt render 800x300 PNG, node-streaming-func.json.txt render 800x380 PNG. Each snippet uses our SDK-style calls and minimal auth (~redwood_api_key placeholder). Add small caption lines for expected latency & streaming note.
- Composite hero tile 1600x480 PNG: small model scroller stacked above request quick-capture on the right and code snippet preview on the left (cropped).

Acceptance criteria:
- Visuals match Figma frames linked below and follow the compact component token spacing.
- No customer/personal data in prompts; all examples use synthetic content.
- Text legible at 90% scale replicating docs thumbnail size. Contrast >= 4.5:1 for body text.
- Assets exported in light and dark theme with file naming convention defined in handoff.
- Final export delivered in PNG and SVG where applicable, plus source Figma file share link.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Chose single-row scroller to save vertical real estate on docs and to be useful inside small console cards. Alternatives considered: condensed grid and dropdown picker. Grid rejected because it consumes vertical space and duplicates existing assets. Dropdown rejected because it doesn't visually communicate model differences quickly.
- Included token-cost microcopy as a static estimate to encourage cost awareness; dynamic real-time cost would be implemented later by engineering, but screenshots should show a plausible estimate to help product copy.
- Streaming toggle in the request composer is shown ON to surface streaming behavior early; we will provide an alternate screenshot with streaming OFF only if requested by PM.

- Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Concise+Launchpad+Screenshot+Spec

Review notes and feedback log (chronological):
- 2026-03-11 — Ava Martinez: Initial comps uploaded to Figma. Focused on compact spacing and token microcopy.
- 2026-03-12 — Priya Shah (PM): "Love the single-row idea—please make cost microcopy more conservative and include a small tooltip indicator icon for 'est. cost'." Added tooltip icon in frame.
- 2026-03-13 — Marco Li (Engineering): "Ensure the scroller can be represented with accessible focus states — share CSS class references for the scroller focus ring." Added note and included color tokens.
- 2026-03-14 — Accessibility review by Hana Kim: "Increase body copy weight to 500 for better contrast at thumbnail scale; avoid 10px font for labels." Updated frames accordingly.
- 2026-03-15 — Design REVIEW (current): Liam O'Connor requested final exports and creation of a tiny animated GIF for the scroller micro-interaction (left chevron scroll). GIF is P3 but requested for marketing; added as optional deliverable.

Blockers / Risks:
- Need final copy for cost microcopy from PM; current text uses placeholder estimates.
- GIF export requires motion spec; motion team syncing required (calendar invite sent).
